answer: Hypothesis (final answer to the question): Original-study effect size estimates tend to be larger than their replications in ALL THREE domains — Social, Cognitive, and Economics — with attenuation of similar magnitude in each. On the Fisher-z scale the original-minus-replication deficit averages about +0.23 to +0.29 depending on the domain (Social median d=0.23, mean 0.23; Cognitive median 0.25, mean 0.29; Economics median 0.14, mean 0.27), and the original effect is larger in magnitude than the replication in ~85% of studies overall (Social 88%, Economics 83%, Cognitive 82%). However, these domain-level differences are statistically indistinguishable: the omnibus permutation test gives F=0.28, p=0.76, every pairwise mean-difference 95% CI straddles 0 (Cognitive vs Economics +0.02 [-0.19, 0.22]; Cognitive vs Social +0.06 [-0.08, 0.19]; Economics vs Social +0.03 [-0.13, 0.22]; Mann-Whitney p ≥ 0.27), so NO domain reliably stands out as having larger original-vs-replication shrinkage — the honest conclusion is "originals larger than replications everywhere, roughly equally". Two nuances: (1) under SE-weighting, the deficit for Cognitive (0.21 [0.12, 0.31]) and Social (0.21 [0.13, 0.28]) remains clearly positive, but for Economics it shrinks to 0.01 [-0.08, 0.20] — i.e., the least-attenuated, most-precisely-replicated Economics (EERP) studies show no detectable deficit, consistent with Economics having the smallest median relative effect (0.70 vs 0.65 Cognitive, 0.13–0.18 Social). (2) Results are robust to the scale choice (correlation scale gives the same ordering: Cognitive 0.25, Social 0.22, Economics 0.20 mean d) and to excluding the 18 sign-flipped replications (deficits shrink but ordering unchanged). If a single-domain emphasis is required, Social psychology shows the most frequent attenuation (largest share of replications smaller than originals, largest share of sign flips, 10/34) and the smallest relative effect sizes, but between-domain differences do not clear conventional significance thresholds. Caveats: domain and replication project are fully confounded (Social & Cognitive come only from the RPP, n=34 each; Economics only from the EERP, n=18), so "domain" effects cannot be separated from project/design effects; Economics n=18 is small, and its wide CIs (e.g., median d CI [0.06, 0.30]) mean its apparent smaller median deficit should not be over-interpreted.

payload.hypothesis: Original-study effect size estimates tend to be larger than replication estimates in all three domains — Social, Cognitive, and Economics — and by a similar amount (mean original-minus-replication deficit on the Fisher-z scale: Cognitive +0.29, Economics +0.27, Social +0.23; originals are larger in magnitude in ~85% of studies: Social 88%, Economics 83%, Cognitive 82%). The domains do not differ reliably from one another (omnibus permutation p=0.76; all pairwise 95% CIs include 0), so the data support 'original effects are larger than replications everywhere' rather than any domain-specific hierarchy. Under precision weighting, the deficit remains clear for Cognitive and Social (~+0.21 each) but is not distinguishable from zero for Economics (+0.01, CI [-0.08, 0.20]), and Economics shows the highest median replication-to-original ratio (0.70 vs 0.65 Cognitive and ~0.13-0.18 Social). Caveat: domain is fully confounded with replication project (Social/Cognitive = RPP only, n=34 each; Economics = EERP only, n=18), so domain and project effects cannot be separated, and the Economics estimate rests on only 18 studies.
payload.workflow: 1) Loaded meta-regression_joined_data_heterogeneity_in_replication_projects.csv (86 rows x 60 cols); verified no duplicate rows/studies and no missing values in key columns; verified fiso=atanh(ro) and fisr=atanh(rr) to machine precision (max dev <1e-9), confirming Fisher-z and correlation scales are interchangeable. 2) Verified algebraic vs absolute comparison coincide on 100% of rows (all originals positive); documented the single relative_es anomaly (B Eitam, RR Hassin, Y Schul: -0.472 vs rr/ro=+0.472) and excluded relative_es as a source of truth, recomputing everything from ro/rr/fiso/fisr. 3) Primary analysis on Fisher-z: per-discipline n, mean and median of d=fiso-fisr with 20,000-resample bootstrap 95% CIs, and share of studies with |fiso|>|fisr|. 4) Between-domain comparisons: pairwise Mann-Whitney U tests, 20,000-permutation tests on mean differences with bootstrap CIs, and an omnibus permutation F-test. 5) Precision-weighted variant (weights 1/(se_fiso^2+se_fisr^2)) reported beside unweighted means. 6) Sensitivity analyses: correlation-scale d (ro-rr), relative_es-based shares with and without fixing the B Eitam sign anomaly, and re-analysis excluding the 18 sign-flipped replications. Script: output/analysis_effect_size_domains.py (seed 42).
